reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Binding ban on lethal autonomous weapons
themes.definition: Concern over weapons with increasing autonomy and calls for a legally binding instrument with prohibitions and restrictions ensuring meaningful human control over the use of force.
themes.inclusion: Passages on killer robots, lethal autonomous weapons systems, machines deciding who lives and dies, or calls for binding rules/bans on them.
themes.exclusion: General human control of AI outside weapons contexts (use AI_HUMAN_CONTROL_OVERSIGHT).
themes.boundary_cases: Rhetorical questions like whether a human or a machine pulls the trigger count here when tied to weapons.

examples.quote: calling for a legally binding instrument with clear prohibitions and restrictions on autonomous weapons
stepping back from creating killing machines — lethal autonomous weapons systems — where an algorithm decides in a split second who lives and who dies
One of the most urgent threats today is the loss of human control over weapons.
Who decides whether a human being or a machine pulls the trigger?

themes.label: Technology must remain under human control
themes.definition: General principle that technology and algorithms must remain under human control and responsibility, beyond specific weapons rules.
themes.inclusion: Passages asserting that algorithms must not decide alone and humans must own responsibility for technology.
themes.boundary_cases: A closing statement mixing weapons and general technology control can take both codes.

examples.quote: Technology must remain under human control. Responsibility must always be owned by us, by humans.

themes.label: Human-centric approach and red lines
themes.definition: New technologies including AI must respect human rights, with a human-centric approach online and offline and ethical red lines.
themes.inclusion: Passages stating human rights apply to new technologies or calling for a human-centric approach to AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Red-line language introducing an autonomous weapons ban takes both codes.

examples.quote: New technologies are not a new frontier where human rights do not exist.
We have to make sure that our human-centric approach applies online and offline.

themes.label: Technologies racing ahead, leaving many behind
themes.definition: Concern that fast-moving technologies such as AI leave many countries or people behind.
themes.inclusion: Passages saying AI and emerging technologies are racing ahead and leaving many behind.
themes.exclusion: Passages focused only on rights or weapons.
themes.boundary_cases: Brief phrasing about being left behind still counts if AI is named.

examples.quote: New and emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum computing are racing ahead, leaving many of us behind.

value.rationale: All passages are Austrian speeches centred on the question of who decides, with autonomous weapons and a binding instrument for human control as the dominant theme; the 2021 passages add human-rights red lines and a human-centric approach, and one notes technology leaving many behind.
